notes: Contract for reconstructing and auditing a Python-oracle baseline. It records requirements, not measurements. No private path, credential, or APK byte belongs in this file.

requiredResultFields.source.revision: Full git revision of the checkout the oracle ran from.
requiredResultFields.source.dirty: True when the worktree differed from the revision.
requiredResultFields.source.headIsExecutedSource: False when dirty; HEAD must not then be treated as the executed source.
requiredResultFields.source.worktreeDigest: Digest covering only executed-source identity: revision, dirty flag, and the dirty/untracked source digest. Policy and manifest digests are separate provenance fields and must not change this value.
requiredResultFields.source.archive.digest: Content digest of the private source archive.
requiredResultFields.source.archive.location: Private archive location, relative to the local migration root.
requiredResultFields.provenance.policySha256: Digest of the pre-registered performance policy.
requiredResultFields.provenance.manifestSha256: Digest of the private runnable corpus manifest.
requiredResultFields.provenance.archiveDigest: Must equal source.archive.digest when archiving succeeded.
requiredResultFields.environment.pythonVersion: Version reported by the pre-synced interpreter, not by uv.
requiredResultFields.environment.gitVersion: Version of git used to record the revision.
requiredResultFields.environment.os/arch: Operating system and CPU architecture of the measurement host.
requiredResultFields.environment.cpuModel/logicalCpus/ramByte: Host capacity, null when the platform query is unsupported.
requiredResultFields.environment.storage: Total/free bytes from df -Pk with its 1024-byte block method recorded.
requiredResultFields.environment.workerCount: Concurrency used by the driver (1 for process-level baseline runs).
requiredResultFields.workload.inputs[].declaredSha256: Hash declared by the private manifest.
requiredResultFields.workload.inputs[].actualSha256: Hash verified before execution; must equal the declared hash.
requiredResultFields.workload.mpp.declaredSha256/actualSha256: Same verification for the Morphe patch bundle.
requiredResultFields.workload.samples[]: Raw samples including warmups, wall time, status, normalized and raw output hashes, optional failed-run diagnostics, and validation errors.
requiredResultFields.workload.outputValidation: Whether stdout/stderr hashes were pinned and whether all outputs validated.
requiredResultFields.acceptance.valid: False for missing required workloads, missing corpus, hash mismatches, unpinned outputs, unsupported required provenance, or a metric whose pre-registered policy budget sets blockOnWorse and that the host cannot collect with tested units. A non-blocking unsupported metric stays null with a reason and must be explained when the policy sets requiresExplanation; it is never recorded as zero.
requiredResultFields.workload.samples[].cpuMs/peakChildRssByt: Measured only when the host exposes the documented unit conversion; null otherwise. Acceptance is blocked when a supported blocking metric is missing from measured samples.

metricRequirements.wallTime: Always supported; measured around spawn through process exit and full stdout/stderr drain.
metricRequirements.cpu: Blocking under the current policy. Linux uses /proc process-tree CPU ticks; macOS sums per-process peak cumulative ps TIME at approximately 10ms display resolution and must not be described as exact.
metricRequirements.descendantRss: Blocking under the current policy. Linux samples /proc RSS; macOS sums ps rss (KiB converted to bytes) over the process group plus parent-linked descendants, and must not be described as aggregate /usr/bin/time maximum single-child RSS.
metricRequirements.io: Non-blocking under the current policy, so an unsupported host reports null with a reason plus an explicit explanation-required limitation. If a future policy sets blockOnWorse, an unsupported metric becomes a hard acceptance blocker.

contents: patches-list.json (release metadata consumed by Morphe reports)
dirty.patch when the worktree differs from the revision
excluded: .venv, target, node_modules, pytest and bytecode caches
reconstruction: Restore the archived files exactly at source.revision.
Do not apply dirty.patch on top: the archive already holds the executed bytes and dirty.patch is evidence of the pre-existing worktree difference.
Verify every file sha256 against the archive manifest.
Run the private corpus manifest through the pre-synced Python interpreter; never install during timing.

sanitization.privateStorage: The runnable manifest, source archive, raw baseline, and any proprietary input identities stay in ignored local storage. A committed result must contain only relative or placeholder paths.
